evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and represents an interpretation from those studies.

claim: The slope of the interspike voltage against the axonal recording distance followed a roughly exponential relationship.
source: A plot of the slope of the interspike voltage against the axonal recording distance followed a roughly exponential relationship with the interspike slope, such that it becomes more shallow with increasing recording distance (Figure 1G; single exponential fit, length constant, λ=211 µm, n=27; R2=0.70; data were fit with a single exponential significantly better than with a line: F(1,24)=22.1, p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1G with statistical analysis.

claim: The main and terminal axons of dopamine neurons are high input resistance compartments in which action potentials are evoked from relatively hyperpolarized interspike voltages.

evidence: This claim represents a summary interpretation of the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: GABA puff resulted in depolarization of the axonal membrane potential by an average of 4.86 ± 0.66 mV.
source: GABA puff resulted in depolarization of the axonal membrane potential by an average of 4.86 ± 0.66 mV (n = 9), which was completely blocked by the GABA-A antagonist picrotoxin (Figure 2C; 100 µM; t(8)=6.1, p=0.0003).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2C with statistical analysis.

claim: GABA-mediated depolarization was completely blocked by the GABA-A antagonist picrotoxin.
source: GABA puff resulted in depolarization of the axonal membrane potential by an average of 4.86 ± 0.66 mV (n = 9), which was completely blocked by the GABA-A antagonist picrotoxin (Figure 2C; 100 µM; t(8)=6.1, p=0.0003).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2C with statistical analysis.

claim: Filling axons with an internal solution containing high chloride resulted in GABA-mediated depolarizations that were 2.76-fold larger in amplitude.
source: We found that filling axons with an internal solution containing high chloride resulted in GABA-mediated depolarizations that were 2.76-fold larger in amplitude (Figure 2D; low Cl-=4.74 ± 0.66 mV, high Cl-=13.1 ± 2.44 mV; t(13)=4.34, p=0.0008).

claim: The reversal potential of axonal GABA-A current was always depolarized relative to the average interspike voltage of the axon.

claim: Muscimol does not alter background striatal dopamine.

claim: The most prominent effect of GABA-A receptor activation was a shortening of the action potential peak.

claim: Larger GABA-induced subthreshold depolarizations result in shorter axonal action potentials.

claim: Direct current injections were significantly less effective at reducing spike peak amplitudes as compared to GABA mediated depolarization.
source: Plotting the spike height against current injection-evoked depolarization in Figure 4D (brown symbols), we found that direct current injections were significantly less effective at reducing spike peak amplitudes as compared to GABA mediated depolarization, shown by a shallower slope of best-fit lines (Figure 4D; GABA-A activation: −1.50 mV/mV, 95% CI: −2.05 to −0.94; direct depolarization: −0.77 mV/mV, 95% CI: −0.96 to −0.59; F(1,25)=4.39, n = 29, p=0.047).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4D with statistical analysis.

claim: There was little difference in the effect of GABA-evoked and direct current injection-evoked depolarization on the rate of rise of axonal action potentials.
source: By contrast, we found little difference in the effect of GABA-evoked and direct current injection-evoked depolarization on the rate of rise of axonal action potentials (dV/dt). Plots in Figure 4E show that both manipulations slowed the rate of rise of action potentials and shared similar dependences on subthreshold depolarization (slope of linear fits; GABA-A activation: −3.78 %/mV 95% CI: −5.46 to −2.10, direct depolarization: −3.20 %/mV, 95% CI: −4.57 to −1.83; F(1,17) = 0.35, n = 21, p=0.56).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4E with statistical analysis.

claim: The peak amplitude of the action potential was susceptible to both depolarizations and shunting inhibition, while the rate of rise was only affected by depolarizations.
source: These data suggested the peak amplitude of the action potential was susceptible to both depolarizations and shunting inhibition, while the rate of rise was only affected by depolarizations.
evidence: This claim represents an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: GABA-A receptor activation had a significantly steeper relationship between change in rate of rise and change in peak spike amplitude compared to direct depolarization.
source: From this relationship the added effect of shunting inhibition is clear in the significantly steeper relationship for GABA-A receptor activation (Figure 4F slope of linear fits; GABA-A activation: 0.44 mV/%, 95% CI: −0.35 to 0.52, direct depolarization: 0.18 mV/mV, 95% CI: 0.15 to 0.22; F (1,17)=39.9, n = 19, p<0.0001).

claim: TTX progressively reduced the amplitude of the peak of the action potential and progressively slowed the rate of rise.

claim: The average effect of TTX was similar to direct depolarization, indicating this effect was mainly through inactivation of sodium channels.

claim: GABA-A receptor activation had a significantly steeper relationship than TTX, revealing the additional contribution of shunting inhibition.

claim: GABA-A receptors act mechanistically through both depolarization of the axonal membrane as well as a change in the input resistance that leads to shunting inhibition.

claim: These two effects combine to slow and shorten dopaminergic action potentials.

claim: Calcium signals in dopaminergic neuron axons of the striatum are most greatly affected by GABA-A receptor activation under conditions involving action potentials that propagate long distances throughout the axonal arbor.

claim: Co-application of GABA-A (gabazine) and GABA-B (CGP-55845) antagonists significantly enhanced dopamine release to 115% of baseline.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B with statistical analysis.

claim: Gabazine alone did not significantly increase dopamine release.
source: We found that co-application of GABA-A (gabazine) and GABA-B (CGP-55845) antagonists significantly enhanced dopamine release to 115% of baseline (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B; t(9)=2.99, p=0.015, n = 10) while gabazine alone did not significantly increase dopamine release (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D).

claim: These results are consistent with previous studies reporting a GABA tone in the striatum.

claim: Diazepam robustly decreased dopamine release in the presence of D2, GABA-B, and muscarinic antagonists.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6A with statistical analysis.

claim: In the presence of nicotinic receptors blocker, diazepam application led to a weaker but still substantial inhibition of dopamine release.

claim: Action potentials in the soma of dopamine neurons are typically broad.

claim: In somatic recordings of pacemaking, dopaminergic neurons exhibit a gradual depolarization of the interspike voltage thought to be critical for the generation of spontaneous activity.
source: In somatic recordings of pacemaking, dopaminergic neurons exhibit a gradual depolarization of the interspike voltage thought to be critical for the generation of spontaneous activity (Kang and Kitai, 1993; Khaliq and Bean, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The slope of the interspike axonal membrane potential was shallow in distal recordings.
source: By contrast, our data from distal recordings show that the slope of the interspike axonal membrane potential was shallow.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from axonal recordings.

claim: The shallower interspike depolarization in the axon suggests that pacemaking in dopaminergic neurons results largely from the intrinsic excitability of the soma and dendrites.
source: The shallower interspike depolarization in the axon suggests that pacemaking in dopaminergic neurons results largely from the intrinsic excitability of the soma and dendrites.

claim: The hyperpolarized axonal threshold potential suggests that the recording site in the axon is distal to the site of action potential initiation, which is the axon initial segment.

claim: These observations argue against the axon as a third site of oscillation generation after the soma and dendrites.
source: Therefore, these observations argue against the axon as a third site of oscillation generation after the soma and dendrites (Pissadaki and Bolam, 2013).

claim: It is possible that the conductances that drive somatic depolarization such as NALCN and HCN may also be present in axons.

claim: A recent study found a positive correlation between the length of the axon initial segment and the spontaneous firing rate.

claim: A different study found that the geometry of the axon initial segment negligibly affects the firing rate.

claim: Large differences exist in the reversal potential of axonal chloride-based conductances when comparing between neuronal cell types.

claim: EGABA shifts from depolarizing to hyperpolarizing with age in cortical layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons, eventually settling at negative values near the somatic resting potential in adult mice.
source: For example, a careful study of the GABA reversal potential in the axon initial segment of cortical layer 2/3 pyramidal neurons demonstrated that EGABA shifts from depolarizing to hyperpolarizing with age, eventually settling at negative values near the somatic resting potential in adult mice (~ −87 mV, Rinetti-Vargas et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Hyperpolarized GABA reversal potential values were reported from proximal axons of layer five pyramidal neurons from rats.

claim: Axonal GABA-A receptors on the mossy fiber bouton have reported depolarizing chloride-based conductances.

claim: The average reversal potential of GABA-mediated currents in dopamine neuron axons, when considered relative to the average axonal interspike membrane potential of −68 mV, is depolarized at −56 mV.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that the average reversal potential of GABA-mediated currents in dopamine neuron axons, when considered relative to the average axonal interspike membrane potential of −68 mV, is also depolarized at −56 mV.

claim: The recordings were performed in adult mice (ages 6–17 weeks, median of 15.5 weeks) suggesting that the depolarized reversal potential represents the value in mature axons.
source: Our recordings were performed in adult mice (ages 6–17 weeks, median of 15.5 weeks) suggesting that the depolarized reversal potential that we obtained represents the value in mature axons.

claim: The reversal potential for somatodendritic GABA currents in dopaminergic neurons is depolarized at −63 mV due to relatively low expression of the K-Cl cotransporter KCC2.
source: Interestingly, the reversal potential for somatodendritic GABA currents in dopaminergic neurons is also depolarized at −63 mV due to relatively low expression of the K-Cl cotransporter KCC2 (Gulácsi et al., 2003), which is similar to the average interspike membrane potential of dopamine neurons during pacemaking.

claim: Activation of somatodendritic GABA-A receptors reduces spiking primarily through shunting with relatively little change in the membrane potential.
source: Therefore, activation of somatodendritic GABA-A receptors reduces spiking primarily through shunting with relatively little change in the membrane potential.

claim: Activation of axonal GABA-A receptors results in inhibition of dopamine release despite the depolarized GABA reversal potential in distal axons.
source: Despite the depolarized GABA reversal potential in distal axons, our findings show that activation of axonal GABA-A receptors results in inhibition of dopamine release.

claim: These results are consistent with work from spinal cord showing inhibitory effects of GABA.

claim: Dopamine neuron axons are among the most branching processes in the brain, forming new bifurcations an average of 31 µm, and possessing an average total length of 467,000 µm.
source: On the other hand, dopamine neuron axons are among the most branching processes in the brain, forming new bifurcations an average of 31 µm, and possessing an average total length of 467,000 µm (Matsuda et al., 2009), from which we can estimate roughly 15,000 total branches per cell.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dopamine neuron axons have roughly 15,000 total branches per cell.
source: On the other hand, dopamine neuron axons are among the most branching processes in the brain, forming new bifurcations an average of 31 µm, and possessing an average total length of 467,000 µm (Matsuda et al., 2009), from which we can estimate roughly 15,000 total branches per cell.

claim: The unusually high frequency of branching may lead to stronger attenuation of propagating spikes.
source: Our data suggests that this unusually high frequency of branching may lead to stronger attenuation of propagating spikes.

claim: Activation of GABA-A receptors had only subtle effects on axonal calcium signals at proximal imaging sites.
source: We found that activation of GABA-A receptors had only subtle effects on axonal calcium signals at proximal imaging sites while axonal calcium signals at distal imaging sites were dramatically reduced.

claim: Axonal calcium signals at distal imaging sites were dramatically reduced by GABA-A receptor activation.
source: We found that activation of GABA-A receptors had only subtle effects on axonal calcium signals at proximal imaging sites while axonal calcium signals at distal imaging sites were dramatically reduced.

claim: GABA-A activation reduces the height of axonal action potentials.
source: We also provide evidence that GABA-A activation reduces the height of axonal action potentials.

claim: The added propagation distance enhances the effects GABA-A receptors in shortening action potentials and depressing dopamine release.

source: In some cases, therefore, the shortening of axonal action potentials may eventually lead to an increase in branch point failures.

claim: Past studies have proposed that presynaptic GABA-A receptors exert their effects through either shunting inhibition or sodium channel inactivation.
source: Past studies have proposed that presynaptic GABA-A receptors exert their effects through either shunting inhibition or sodium channel inactivation (Trigo et al., 2008).

claim: In the rat posterior pituitary nerve terminals, GABA was shown to produce large depolarizations that led to strong inactivation of sodium channels, while shunting was thought to play little role in inhibition of secretion from terminals.
source: In the rat posterior pituitary nerve terminals, GABA was shown to produce large depolarizations that led to strong inactivation of sodium channels, while shunting was thought to play little role in inhibition of secretion from terminals (Zhang and Jackson, 1993).

claim: In the thin, unmyelinated axons of dopaminergic neurons, shunting and depolarization-mediated inactivation of sodium channels contribute nearly equally to GABA-A receptor mediated alteration of action potential shape and the subsequent inhibition of striatal dopamine release.
source: Here, we demonstrate in the thin, unmyelinated axons of dopaminergic neurons that shunting and depolarization-mediated inactivation of sodium channels contribute nearly equally to GABA-A receptor mediated alteration of action potential shape and the subsequent inhibition of striatal dopamine release.

claim: Under conditions of tonic GABA-A receptor activation, the two inhibitory mechanisms will be especially prominent, particularly in an electrically tight compartment like the axon.
source: Under conditions of tonic GABA-A receptor activation, these two inhibitory mechanisms will be especially prominent, particularly in an electrically tight compartment like the axon where tiny fluctuations of GABA-A activity can cause large changes in membrane voltage and input resistance.
evidence: This claim represents an inference about the functional implications of the findings.

claim: Depolarization-mediated sodium channel inactivation both reduces spike height and slows the rate of action potential rise.
source: Furthermore, we found that these two mechanisms of inhibition differentially affect action potential waveforms. While depolarization-mediated sodium channel inactivation both reduces spike height and slows the rate of action potential rise, shunting inhibition only affects spike height.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Shunting inhibition only affects spike height.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The rewarding actions of benzodiazepines are thought to involve potentiation of GABA-A receptors located on inhibitory GABAergic neuron within the VTA which then results in disinhibition of VTA dopaminergic neurons.
source: The rewarding actions of benzodiazepines are thought to involve potentiation of GABA-A receptors located on inhibitory GABAergic neuron within the VTA which then results in disinhibition of VTA dopaminergic neurons (Tan et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Drugs that disinhibit dopamine neurons would be expected to increase the somatic firing rate and subsequent dopamine release in the striatum.
source: As is the case with other drugs of abuse that disinhibit dopamine neurons (e.g. opioids), benzodiazepines would be expected then to increase the somatic firing rate and subsequent dopamine release in the striatum.
evidence: This claim represents an inference based on established knowledge about drugs of abuse.

claim: Studies of awake behaving rats show that systemic diazepam administration increases the frequency of dopamine release events but decreases the amplitude of these release events.
source: Instead, studies of awake behaving rats show that systemic diazepam administration increases the frequency of dopamine release events but decreases the amplitude of these release events (Schelp et al., 2018).

claim: The apparent disparity in benzodiazepine effects can be reconciled by the observation that axonal GABA-A receptors on dopaminergic neuron axons are enhanced by diazepam.
source: The apparent disparity in these results can be reconciled by our observation that axonal GABA-A receptors on dopaminergic neuron axons are enhanced by diazepam.

claim: Enhancement of GABA-A receptors by diazepam leads to a decrease in dopamine release through a combination of shunting inhibition and depolarization-mediated sodium channel inactivation.
source: This enhancement of GABA-A receptors leads to a decrease in dopamine release through a combination of shunting inhibition and depolarization-mediated sodium channel inactivation.

claim: The effects of drugs that pharmacologically target GABA-A receptors such as ethanol, barbiturates, and other sedatives should be reexamined considering their potential effects on axonal GABA-A receptors.

claim: Most compounds that target GABA-A receptors are not direct agonists, but rather positive allosteric modulators.
source: Of note, most of these compounds that target GABA-A receptors are not direct agonists, but rather positive allosteric modulators.

claim: Diazepam has been shown to both increase single channel conductance of GABA-A receptors and increase receptor affinity for GABA.

claim: Diazepam does not induce substantial receptor opening, but instead enhances the affinity and efficacy of orthosteric agonists.
source: Therefore, diazepam does not induce substantial receptor opening, but instead enhances the affinity and efficacy of orthosteric agonists, an effect that may depend on novel GABA-A receptor auxiliary subunits (Han et al., 2019).

claim: GABA-A receptors are well established to exhibit tonic activity, as shown by a change in holding current and a reduction in the recording RMS noise while in voltage clamp.
source: GABA-A receptors are well established to exhibit tonic activity, as shown by a change in holding current and a reduction in the recording RMS noise while in voltage clamp (Semyanov et al., 2004).

claim: Blockade of GABA-A receptors with gabazine has little effect on dopamine release under control conditions.

claim: Following application of diazepam, there is a significant reduction in input resistance of dopaminergic neuron axons.

claim: The experiments showing diazepam effects on input resistance were performed in the absence of electrical or optical stimulation which argues strongly for the involvement of GABA tone in the diazepam-mediated inhibition of striatal dopamine.
